MarioFanaticXV wrote:
 Silverleaf wrote:
How is asking to see characters other than straight white cis males "demanding pandering"? Straight white cis males are hugely overrepresented in every genre. I don't see why people being happy that a character is a bit like them in a world where they are almost invisible in the media is in any way a bad thing.And you say SWJ like that's a bad thing too. On the contrary, we can tell more interesting stories with more diverse characters.It's interesting to me that most of the people who use SWJ as a pejorative term criticise anyone asking for characters that represent them, while themselves getting terribly upset whenever a character isn't just like them. 
...And you seem to have completely misread what I said. Firstly, no one even mentioned straight white males, but the fact that you jump right on that is the typical bigotry of which I was worried about. Secondly, no one was complaining about people other than that being included. I was complaining about pandering, which is hugely different. Thirdly, the point I was making was that we shouldn't need a character to be just like us to enjoy a game; honestly, if a game character was just like me, I wouldn't bother- I spend enough time being me in real life, I don't need that in a game. Fourthly, no one was complaining about diversity; once again, this makes me question if you even read the post I made beyond the first few words.
Silverleaf isn't being bigoted. The reason she brought up straight white dudes is that she made a comment about Parse not being a straight white dude earlier in the thread and you responded with a comment about SJW bigotry. You later produced a straw man about how so-called "SJWs" want pandering and not fully realized characters, which is 180 degrees from anything I've ever seen in the real world. If you want to complain about pandering, it'd help to have actual instances of a) pandering and b) people demanding pandering to talk about. Since neither is in evidence here, why are you so worried about it?

Thanks Belle. I tend to respond negatively to someone who uses a pejorative term (SJW) for anyone who would prefer representation and accuses people of "demanding pandering" when no one has done that.

It's very common to hear things like "You SJWs just want to ruin everything! If we include women and gays and blacks it'll make everything SUCK!". "SJW" is a term designed to belittle anyone expressing liberal or progressive views so you don't have to listen to them any more. Just like calling someone a "hater". I hear anyone using SJW in a serious way, I assume they are a Gamergate bottom-feeder, because it's a Gamergate buzzword.

Of course, it's very easy to say that you shouldn't need characters to represent you when 95%* of characters already do represent you. (And 4% are horrible stereotypes of marginalised groups, and/or sex objects.) I am extremely pleased that Sentinels doesn't follow the norm here.

 

  • I made that number up. It feels like that though, speaking as a person who is non-male, non-straight, and non-cis, it can be extremely difficult to find a character who I have anything in common with. And if you experience that enough, you start hearing "Games. Are. Not. For. You."

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
MarioFanaticXV:

My apologies; I'll say one last thing and drop the subject: I felt that the fact they couldn't describe us as "abnormal" was… Quite frankly insulting. Especially since "abnormal" in and of itself doesn't even carry any negative connotations, just "different". And if we can't accept we're different, how can we expect anyone else to? It's this type of thing that worried me, as it tends to be more divisive than anything, and feels like those that typically make such comments are the very thing they claim to be against…But I'll go ahead and stop here; this really isn't the place to be discussing this, it just struck a nerve is all. Sorry for any interuptions it may have caused.

"Abnormal" totally has negative connotations. I don't have any problems with acknowledging differences between people, and I wasn't in any way trying to say that people with autism (or any other group) are exactly the same as people without autism. I have a cognitive disability myself but I would hate for anyone to describe me as "abnormal".

My point was that many people with Asperger's don't consider themselves to have a disability and argue that the differences we see are just a spectrum of thought patterns and behaviours that don't need to be classified as normal/disordered because that variance itself is normal. It's not my place to label those people in a way they dislike, which is why I don't like to use "neurotypical" as it sets up non-disabled as the "ideal" and disabled as "other" or "non-ideal".

I apologise if I've upset you with that, but believe me that my intentions were to avoid upsetting people by using a term I know to be problematic.

I've been playing around with a spreadsheet to try to get a guessimate of how the KS will do, when it'll hit a million, etc. It looks at multi-day trends (and then multi-day trending of the trends) to predict the next day's pledge amount, and then uses the trend-of-the-trend to project further into the timeline. Like Kicktraq it's wildly inaccurate at the start, but I believe mine gets better at a faster pace than Kicktraq (which still thinks OblivAeon will hit 2.5 million, which would be great, but seriously???).

Anyway, early on in had 750K all the out at 3 March and little to no hope of 1 million. By yesterday, the magic day for 1 million was next week Tuesday, with a final total of 1.3 million.

Yesterday's total, though, was lower than projected.  Plugging in yesterday's total, the trends recalculated and pushed the 1 million day out to the 28th, with a final total at 1.06 million.

What this does NOT account for:
        Friday bumps as people get paid and set aside money before pledging
        weekend dips, though the multi-day trending levels that out (somewhat)
       the final 48 hour jump that many KS see

This is all just my ridiculously long-winded way of saying, I still think we'll get to 1 million, but I don't feel the need to check the KS total every 5 minutes.

As you were...
